title: Do Better Scores Mean Better Physics? Physics-Grounded Explanations for Sim2Real Neural Operators
abstract: arXiv:2610.00415v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Machine-learning surrogates accelerate physical simulation, but lower prediction error need not coincide with lower error in physically relevant flow statistics. We examine this question for flow around a NACA4418 airfoil using paired computational-fluid-dynamics simulations and experimental particle-image-velocimetry measurements. A mean-preserving input intervention removes velocity fluctuations from selected regions of observed flow histories. Across four neural operators, removing fluctuations from the most energetic 10% of valid observed cells changes forecasts more than equal-area random removal. Because the masks are not matched for removed fluctuation energy, this contrast measures sensitivity, not independent evidence of physical importance. translated_title: 更好的分数意味着更好的物理吗？面向Sim2Real神经算子的物理基础解释
translated_abstract: 机器学习代理模型加速了物理模拟，但更低的预测误差并不一定等同于在物理相关的流动统计量上具有更低的误差。我们利用配对的计算流体动力学（CFD）模拟与实验性粒子图像测速（PIV）测量，针对NACA4418翼型绕流研究了这一问题。我们采用一种保持均值的输入干预方法，从观测流动历史的选定区域中移除速度脉动。在四个神经算子上，从有效观测单元中能量最高的10%区域移除脉动，比等面积的随机移除对预测结果的改变更大。但由于这些掩码在所移除的脉动能量上并未匹配，这种对比衡量的是模型的敏感性，而非物理重要性的独立证据。另外，在两个分析子集上，CNO的速度场误差低于参考基准，但其两分量脉动能量误差却显著更高。一项输出衰减压力测试……
tldr: 该论文通过配对CFD-PIV数据与保持均值的输入干预实验，揭示了神经算子更低的预测误差并不等同于更好的物理保真度（例如CNO速度场误差更低但脉动能量统计误差显著更高），为Sim2Real神经算子提供了基于物理的解释框架。
en_tdlr: Using paired CFD-PIV experiments and mean-preserving input interventions, this paper shows that lower prediction error of neural operators does not imply better fidelity to physically relevant flow statistics, providing physics-grounded explanations for Sim2Real neural operators.
